elements.element: No liquidated damages are payable by Customer under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 7.6 states that “Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages ... under this Agreement.”

elements.element: No penalties are payable by Customer under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 7.6 states that “Customer shall not be liable for any ... penalties under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer is capped at three months’ fees.
elements.evidence: The clause categorically eliminates Customer liability for all liquidated damages and penalties, so no early-termination fee is payable; zero liability is within the three-month cap.

elements.element: No liquidated amount other than the capped early-termination fee is payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause prohibits all liquidated damages payable by Customer, and therefore necessarily prohibits every liquidated amount other than a permitted early-termination fee.

result.reason: The operative redline fully achieves the preferred position by eliminating all Customer liability for liquidated damages and penalties throughout the Agreement. It also satisfies the fallback because the broader prohibition leaves no early-termination fee exceeding three months’ fees and no other liquidated amount. The change is concise, removes the original USD 25,000-per-day charge, and adds no unrelated obligation. The non-operative margin comment is not relied upon.
